function.mechanism: Acidifies foods and lowers pH; undissociated acid fraction suppresses growth of susceptible microbes and contributes sourness/flavor balance.
common_food_categories: foods using antimicrobial acidulation under GMP (excluding infant foods/formulas in 21 CFR 184.1061)

adi.basis: No finalized EFSA numerical ADI identified for E270; EFSA re-evaluation record EFSA-Q-2011-00596 is ongoing/planned with no published output yet.

efsa.key_finding: OpenEFSA record (last modified 2026-01-19) states E270 is already authorised in the EU, re-evaluation has been delayed, and a new call for data is planned in 2026.

adi.basis: JECFA page reports ADI as 'NOT LIMITED (1973)' (qualitative, non-numeric).

concerns.summary: Recent human literature links D-lactic acidosis mainly to vulnerable patients (short bowel syndrome/intestinal failure), where carbohydrate fermentation and D-lactate accumulation can cause neurologic symptoms and metabolic acidosis.
A current EFSA final re-evaluation output specific to E270 was not identified (ongoing process), creating a data-gap for modern EU exposure refinement.

no_concern_confirmed: FDA affirms lactic acid as GRAS for direct food use under GMP conditions (21 CFR 184.1061).
JECFA records ADI as NOT LIMITED (1973) and notes no safety concern at current flavouring-use intake.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric EFSA ADI and qualitative JECFA ADI limit direct exceedance calculation; risk discussion is population-specific rather than general-population ADI exceedance.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evidence indicates low concern at normal use levels (FDA GRAS, JECFA not-limited ADI), but a finalized EFSA E270 re-evaluation is pending and vulnerable clinical subgroups can develop D-lactic acidosis under specific conditions.
key_factors: E270 already authorised in EU per EFSA question comment but re-evaluation output pending
FDA GRAS with GMP conditions and infant-food/formula exclusion in 21 CFR 184.1061
JECFA ADI reported as NOT LIMITED (1973), evaluation year listed as 2001
No IARC classification entry found for lactic acid/CAS 50-21-5
Recent PubMed safety signals concentrated in short bowel/intestinal failure populations
